text: The exec team needs to see how the practice is doing, without any risk of changing something. That's the Executive role.
The one thing to remember: an executive sees every report and Marketing, and changes nothing, unless you grant them Marketing edit rights.
This is Blair, on the exec team. Marketing is here. Settings and Admin aren't.
There's no booking or new-client button on the left. Executives read; they don't book.
Blair can read campaigns and their results, but there's no New campaign button.
Executives can open client records to read them, but the buttons that change things, like Deactivate or Send reset password, aren't there.
To let one executive edit campaigns and promotions, a practice admin grants them that one permission on their Access tab.
The most common mistake is giving an exec an admin login just to see reports. The Executive role shows everything, without the risk.
Remember: executives see every report and Marketing, and change nothing unless you grant Marketing edit rights.
